To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the changes in the values of P12 and beta12 can be used to detect the changes in the frequency of N3 discharges or in the amplitude of the postsynaptic potentials excited by these discharges.

the increase in the degree of dependence P12 of the impulse activity trains of two neurons, monosynaptical excited by the third one, is accompanied by a decrease in the mean interimpulse interval of the third neuron and/or an increase in the amplitude of the postsynaptic potential elicited by its discharges.

the analysis of P12, P1*, P1* and beta 12 values allows to detect plastic changes in the activity of the neurones monosynapticaly excited by a third neurone, and to distinguish the plasticity of the neurone discharges frequency from the plasticity of amplitude of excited postsyntaptic potentials.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a method of mathematical modeling exogenic stationary random impulse trains of two neurones monosynaptical excited by a third neurone.
the possibility of detecting neuronal and synaptic changes in the central nervous system on the basis of cross-correlation histograms analysis and of Cox's method application.
the potential of cross-correlation histograms analysis for the study of synaptic plasticity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
P12 and beta 12 are the most reliable and sensitive parameters to detect plastic changes in impulse activity of the monosynaptical neurones and in the efficiency of their synaptic contacts.

the changes in the values of the P1*, P1*, P3* and beta 12 coefficients, as a result of the changes in the excitability of the neurons and the efficiency of the interneuronal links, can be considered as a sign of the plastic changes of the neurons and synapses.

the increase or decrease of P12 or of beta 12 accompanied with the decrease or increase of P3*, P12 or beta12 is a sign of the plastic change of N3 discharges, and the decrease or increase P1* and/or P2*, accompanied by the increase or decrease P3* is a sign that plastic change has been occurred in the amplitude of excited PSPs elicited by the N3 discharges.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the analysis of P12 and beta 12 values can be used as a method for the evaluation of neuronal and synaptic plastic changes.
the value beta 12 is the more sensitive indicator of plastic changes of interneurone connections.

the analysis of the dynamics of P12 and beta 12 is an effective way to evaluate the dynamics of the efficiency of interneurons connections, the dynamics of their excitability, and the dynamics of summate action on neurones of independent random aferent synaptic inflows.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the analysis of the impulse activities of two monosynapticaly excitable neurones using cross-correlation histogram is a method to evaluate the efficiency of the interneuronal connection and to study the dynamics of plastic changes of its parameters, and that this analysis is more informative than the analysis of the mean values of the interimpulse intervals.
the method of mathematical modelling of neurones impulse activity is effective to study the neuronal and synaptic plastic changes in the brain.

the changes in the degree of N1 andN2 dependence can be used as a criterion of changes of the efficiency of interneuron connections, or of the changes of N3 discharge frequency, or of the plastic changes of postsynaptic potentials amplitudes elicited by N3 discharges.
